`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

# Interpolate where a fitted curve crosses ratio = 1 (dentin density).
#
# Takes the LAST upward crossing after which the curve stays above 1, not the
# first time it touches. A wiggle in the steep crossover region can nick 1.0 and
# fall back; anchoring on that gives a crossover several % early and, at a curve
# end, can latch onto a spurious edge crossing entirely.
#
# Returns NA when the curve never rises above 1 and stays there. For a severely
# hypomineralized specimen that is the correct answer, not a failure.
crossing_of <- function(z, fit) {
  above <- fit >= 1
  idx   <- which(diff(above) == 1)
  if (length(idx) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  i <- idx[length(idx)]
  for (j in rev(idx)) {
    if (all(above[(j + 1):length(above)])) i <- j
  }
  z[i] + (1 - fit[i]) * (z[i + 1] - z[i]) / (fit[i + 1] - fit[i])
}

# Mean fitted ratio over the mature plateau window.
plateau_of <- function(z, fit) mean(fit[z >= 70 & z <= 95], na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Overview

The mouse incisor grows continuously, so its **length is a developmental time axis**: tissue at the
cervical loop (`z = 0 %`) was deposited most recently, tissue at the incisal tip (`z = 100 %`) is
fully mature. A density profile along that axis therefore traces the whole of amelogenesis in a
single specimen — secretory matrix, through maturation, to mature enamel.

This report pools every specimen that has a CMPR resliced volume and runs **three comparisons plus
one developmental reference**:

| # | Comparison | Contrast isolated | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P82 WT vs P82 CFTR cKO** | genotype, age-matched | §9 |
| 2 | **P52 WT vs P52 Hif1a cKO** | genotype, age-matched | §10 |
| 3 | **P82 WT vs P52 WT** | age, genotype-matched | §11 |
| — | **Odam-Cre WT development curve** | wildtype reference, fitted per age | §12 |

Every animal carries the Odam-Cre driver, including all wildtype groups, so the driver is not a
variable anywhere in this dataset. Each knockout is compared only against its **age-matched**
wildtype, and the age comparison uses only wildtype animals. No figure mixes a genotype difference
with an age difference.

**Age is never pooled.** It is the largest driver of the developmental pattern here, so every
quantity that describes a trajectory — the wildtype development curve in §12, the anatomical
landmark consensus in §7, the crossover and plateau landmarks — is computed within an age and
reported per age. Landmarks are matched on age alone: a knockout of enamel mineralization does not
move the molars or the eruption plane, so within an age the same landmark set serves every genotype.

**The plotted quantity is the enamel/dentin ratio.** Raw intensities are scanner units, not
mg HA/cm³, and are not comparable across scan sessions; dentin is the shared internal reference
tissue, so the ratio is self-calibrating.

**The z axis carries anatomy.** [`map_landmarks.py`](../map_landmarks.py) maps the eruption plane
and the three molar positions onto the same `z_percent` axis the density profile uses, so positions
on the curve can be named rather than only numbered. Every trajectory figure carries that anatomy
strip beneath it.

> **Naming.** All files were renamed on 2026-09-17 to `{Age}_{BaseMouse}_{Gene}_{N}`. The CFTR
> specimens were previously called `P82-OdamcKo-CTR-*` — a name that reads as a control — inside a
> folder named `NATARA-P82-CFTR`. `sample_rename_map.csv` on the Z drive maps every old path to its
> new one.

## 1. Load every profile with a CMPR volume

Each specimen contributes one `*_enamel_density_profile.csv` (one row per z-slice) and one
`*_enamel_density_run.json` of provenance. Files are discovered rather than hard-coded, but a
specimen is admitted only if it also has a CMPR resliced volume.

```{r discover}
csv_files <- list.files(params$results_dir,
                        pattern = "_enamel_density_profile\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
# macOS AppleDouble sidecars ("._name.csv") are not data.
csv_files <- csv_files[!str_starts(basename(csv_files), stringr::fixed("._"))]

json_files <- list.files(params$results_dir,
                         pattern = "_enamel_density_run\\.json$", full.names = TRUE)
json_files <- json_files[!str_starts(basename(json_files), stringr::fixed("._"))]

# The CMPR directory is the roster: a specimen without a resliced volume is not
# analyzed even if a stale profile CSV exists for it.
cmpr_files   <- list.files(params$cmpr_dir, pattern = "_resliced_volume\\.nrrd$")
cmpr_files   <- cmpr_files[!str_starts(cmpr_files, stringr::fixed("._"))]
cmpr_samples <- str_remove(cmpr_files, "_resliced_volume\\.nrrd$")

landmark_dirs  <- unique(params$landmark_dirs %||% params$results_dir)
landmark_dirs  <- landmark_dirs[dir.exists(landmark_dirs)]
landmark_files <- unlist(lapply(landmark_dirs, list.files,
                                pattern = "_landmarks\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE))
landmark_files <- landmark_files[!str_starts(basename(landmark_files),
                                             stringr::fixed("._"))]
landmark_files <- landmark_files[!duplicated(basename(landmark_files))]

stopifnot(length(csv_files) > 0)

profile_samples  <- str_remove(basename(csv_files), "_enamel_density_profile\\.csv$")
landmark_samples <- str_remove(basename(landmark_files), "_landmarks\\.csv$")

roster <- tibble(sample = sort(union(cmpr_samples, profile_samples))) |>
  mutate(`CMPR volume`     = sample %in% cmpr_samples,
         `density profile` = sample %in% profile_samples,
         landmarks         = sample %in% landmark_samples,
         analyzed          = `CMPR volume` & `density profile`)

roster
```

```{r load}
read_profile <- function(path) {
  sample_id <- str_remove(basename(path), "_enamel_density_profile\\.csv$")

  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
      sample  = sample_id,
      # Everything downstream is numeric; the writer emits "" for unfit rows.
      across(
        c(z, z_percent, z_mm, n_voxels, z_window, rim_fraction,
          dentin_mode, dentin_reference, enamel_density, enamel_sigma,
          enamel_ratio, enamel_fraction, separation_sigma, solidity),
        ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))
      )
    )
}

# Gate on CMPR presence before reading anything.
csv_files <- csv_files[profile_samples %in% cmpr_samples]
profiles  <- map(csv_files, read_profile) |> list_rbind()
```

### Specimen metadata

```{r metadata}
meta <- str_split_fixed(unlist(params$specimens), "\\|", 3) |>
  as_tibble(.name_repair = ~ c("sample", "genotype", "age")) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), str_trim))

missing_meta <- setdiff(unique(profiles$sample), meta$sample)
if (length(missing_meta) > 0) {
  stop("No metadata for: ", paste(missing_meta, collapse = ", "),
       ". Add them to the `specimens` block in the YAML header.")
}

# `group` is the analysis unit throughout: genotype crossed with age. The level
# order places each knockout immediately after the wildtype it is tested against.
group_levels <- c("WT P52", "Hif1a cKO P52", "WT P82", "CFTR cKO P82")

# Every status enamel_density.py can emit. factor() turns an unlisted level
# into NA silently, which would drop those slices from every filter and count
# below without a word, so the set is asserted rather than assumed: if the
# pipeline gains a status, this report stops instead of quietly ignoring it.
status_levels <- c("resolved_hi", "resolved_lo", "coincident", "pre_onset",
                   "saturated", "insufficient", "unresolvable")

unknown_status <- setdiff(unique(profiles$status), status_levels)
if (length(unknown_status)) {
  stop("Unknown status in the profile CSVs: ",
       paste(unknown_status, collapse = ", "),
       ". Add it to `status_levels` and decide how sections 2, 3 and 5 should ",
       "treat it before rerunning.")
}

# Guard against knitting over a half-finished `run_all.sh`. A `pre_onset` slice
# carries enamel_ratio = 0 by construction; a non-zero one means that CSV was
# written by an older build of enamel_density.py, and mixing pipeline versions
# across specimens would put a processing difference into every between-group
# comparison in this report.
stale <- profiles |>
  filter(status == "pre_onset", !is.na(enamel_ratio), enamel_ratio != 0) |>
  distinct(sample) |>
  pull(sample)
if (length(stale)) {
  stop("These profiles predate the enamel-onset change: ",
       paste(stale, collapse = ", "),
       ". Let run_all.sh finish, then re-knit.")
}

profiles <- profiles |>
  left_join(meta, by = "sample") |>
  mutate(
    genotype = factor(genotype, levels = c("WT", "Hif1a cKO", "CFTR cKO")),
    age      = factor(age, levels = c("P52", "P82")),
    group    = factor(paste(genotype, age), levels = group_levels),
    status   = factor(status, levels = status_levels)
  )

# Shared colour key. Wildtype groups are blues/greens (same genotype, different
# age); each knockout is a warm colour that sits next to its own control.
group_cols <- c("WT P52"        = "#2166AC",
                "Hif1a cKO P52" = "#B2182B",
                "WT P82"        = "#4DAF9A",
                "CFTR cKO P82"  = "#E08214")

meta |>
  filter(sample %in% unique(profiles$sample)) |>
  mutate(group = paste(genotype, age)) |>
  arrange(group, sample) |>
  select(group, genotype, age, sample)
```

excluded     <- params$exclude_samples %||% character(0)
profiles_all <- profiles                       # kept for the landmark depth lookup
profiles     <- profiles |> filter(!sample %in% excluded)
```

n_wt52  <- n_by("WT P52")

### Per-specimen slice outcomes

`enamel_density.py` labels every slice with the outcome of its two-component histogram fit. That
composition is itself a readout, and section 3 shows it is **not** ignorable here.

```{r status-table}
status_tbl <- profiles |>
  count(group, sample, status, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(group))

status_tbl |>
  select(group, sample, status, pct) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  arrange(group, sample)
```

```{r fig-status, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Slice-outcome composition per specimen. `pre_onset` is the pre-enamel zone at the cervical loop, cervical to the density minimum that marks the start of secretory matrix; those slices contain no enamel and are separated from `coincident`, which is enamel that exists but cannot be resolved from dentin. Section 3 shows the coincident excess in CFTR is a phenotype, not a processing artifact."}
ggplot(status_tbl, aes(x = sample, y = pct, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_grid(group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu", direction = -1, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of slices", fill = NULL) +
  theme_prism(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

## 2. Quality filtering

Filters, each from a documented caveat in the pipeline README:

1. **Measurable statuses only.** `resolved_hi`, `resolved_lo` and `coincident` carry a density;
   `unresolvable` / `insufficient` do not.
   `pre_onset` is excluded here for a different reason, and the distinction matters. Those
   slices lie cervical to the start of enamel — the cross-section is dentin plus enamel-organ
   soft tissue, with no enamel in it — so the pipeline reports `enamel_ratio = 0`, meaning
   *none of it*, not *could not measure*. That zero is a true value but it is not a point on
   the mineralization curve, and leaving it in would drag every group mean and GAM fit toward
   0 across the cervical decile. Section 9 uses its **prevalence** instead, where the
   extent of the pre-enamel zone is the quantity of interest.
2. **`z_window` cap.** A wide pooling window means that point traded z-resolution for histogram
   signal.
3. **`solidity` floor on `resolved_lo` rows.** This is the primary evidence that a low-density
   component is real secretory matrix rather than partial-volume rim — genuine matrix scores
   ≥ 0.10, rim scores 0.00–0.01.

```{r qc}
measured <- profiles |>
  filter(
    status %in% c("resolved_hi", "resolved_lo", "coincident"),
    z_window <= params$max_z_window,
    !(status == "resolved_lo" & (is.na(solidity) | solidity < 0.10))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(enamel_ratio))

# Belt and braces on the pre-enamel zero. The status whitelist above already
# excludes `pre_onset`, but a ratio of exactly 0 is never a measurement of
# enamel anywhere in this pipeline, and if one ever reaches the smoother it
# would pull a group mean down by a full ratio unit while looking like data.
stopifnot(!any(measured$enamel_ratio == 0, na.rm = TRUE))

bind_rows(
  profiles |> mutate(stage = "all slices"),
  measured |> mutate(stage = "after QC")
) |>
  group_by(group, stage) |>
  summarise(slices = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = slices) |>
  mutate(`% retained` = round(100 * `after QC` / `all slices`, 1)) |>
  select(group, `all slices`, `after QC`, `% retained`)
```

---

## 3. What a `coincident` slice is, and why it is not forced to 1.0

**This section changes a rule the previous version of this report used, and the change matters most
for the group the report was rebuilt to analyze.**

A slice is labelled `coincident` when the enamel and dentin histogram modes are too close to
separate at the configured confidence. The previous rule treated that as a *measurement* of "enamel
equals dentin" and overwrote the ratio with exactly 1.0, on the reasoning that dropping the slices
would delete the crossover. That reasoning holds when `coincident` is rare and confined to the
crossover. It fails here.

**One class of `coincident` slice has been removed upstream since the previous version of this
report.** `enamel_density.py` now identifies the enamel onset — the profile's density minimum,
which is the secretory matrix, the least mineralized enamel on the tooth — and relabels everything
cervical to it as `pre_onset`. Those slices used to be reported as `coincident` with a ratio near
1.03, which asserted that enamel was present at dentin density; in fact there is no enamel there at
all, only dentin and enamel-organ soft tissue at a coincidentally similar attenuation. The counts
below are therefore smaller than in the previous run, and the ones that remain are `coincident` in
the sense this section is about: enamel that exists but cannot be separated from dentin. The
distinction sharpens the argument rather than weakening it — the cervical bins no longer mix a
detection failure with a region that has nothing to detect.

```{r coincident-where}
profiles |>
  filter(status == "coincident") |>
  mutate(bin = cut(z_percent, breaks = seq(0, 100, 10),
                   labels = sprintf("%d–%d", seq(0, 90, 10), seq(10, 100, 10)),
                   include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  count(group, bin) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

In wildtype, `coincident` sits where it should — a thin band at the crossover. In **CFTR cKO it is
spread across the whole maturation zone**, because that is where knockout enamel and dentin
genuinely have similar densities. Those slices are not all failed crossover fits.

The test that decides the rule: for each `coincident` slice, compare its own fitted ratio against
the local median of nearby **resolved** slices in the same specimen. If forcing 1.0 were harmless,
that neighbourhood would already sit near 1.

```{r coincident-neighbours}
neighbour_check <- measured |>
  arrange(sample, z) |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  group_modify(function(d, key) {
    res <- d$status %in% c("resolved_hi", "resolved_lo")
    ci  <- which(d$status == "coincident")
    if (length(ci) == 0) return(tibble())
    map_dfr(ci, function(i) {
      m <- abs(d$z - d$z[i]) <= 25 & res
      if (sum(m) < 5) return(tibble())
      tibble(own = d$enamel_ratio[i],
             nbr = median(d$enamel_ratio[m], na.rm = TRUE))
    })
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(meta, by = "sample") |>
  mutate(group = factor(paste(genotype, age), levels = group_levels))

neighbour_check |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    `n coincident`        = n(),
    `median own ratio`    = round(median(own, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `median neighbour`    = round(median(nbr, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `% neighbours > 1.10` = round(100 * mean(nbr > 1.10, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

**In CFTR cKO roughly half of all `coincident` slices sit in a neighbourhood whose resolved slices
are already well above 1.1.** Forcing those to 1.0 does not record "enamel equals dentin" — it pulls
a real, measurably-above-dentin stretch of curve down onto the reference line.

The arithmetic consequence, per group, as the largest distortion any z-bin suffers:

```{r coincident-impact}
bin_curve <- function(rule) {
  d <- measured
  if (rule == "force1") {
    d <- d |> mutate(enamel_ratio = if_else(status == "coincident", 1, enamel_ratio))
  } else if (rule == "drop") {
    d <- d |> filter(status != "coincident")
  }
  d |>
    mutate(bin = cut(z_percent, breaks = seq(0, 100, 5), include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
    group_by(group, bin) |>
    summarise(v = median(enamel_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(rule = rule)
}

impact <- bind_rows(bin_curve("measured"), bin_curve("force1"), bin_curve("drop")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = v) |>
  filter(!is.na(measured))

impact |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    `max |force1 - measured|` = round(max(abs(force1 - measured), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `max |drop - measured|`   = round(max(abs(drop   - measured), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Both alternatives distort, in opposite directions. `force1` flattens the curve onto 1.0; dropping
the slices biases it *upward*, by deleting the lowest-density measurements in a region where they
are real. **Neither is neutral, so this report keeps the measured ratio** and treats the
*prevalence* of `coincident` as a phenotype readout in its own right (section 9).

```{r coincident-apply}
if (params$coincident_rule == "force1") {
  measured <- measured |>
    mutate(enamel_ratio = if_else(status == "coincident", 1, enamel_ratio))
} else if (params$coincident_rule == "drop") {
  measured <- measured |> filter(status != "coincident")
}
```

---

## 4. Outlier rejection, kept separate from smoothing

These two are routinely conflated. They address different defects, and the distinction is
load-bearing here:

- An **outlier** is a slice whose two-component fit landed on the wrong mode. It is *wrong*, and
  averaging it in corrupts its neighbourhood. It must be removed.
- **Noise** is the small slice-to-slice scatter of correct measurements. It is *right but
  imprecise*, and smoothing is the correct response.

Confusing them is dangerous in both directions: rejecting real structure as outliers deletes
biology, and smoothing a genuinely discontinuous curve manufactures continuity that was never
measured.

### The measurement noise is tiny, and uniform across groups

```{r noise-scale}
noise_tbl <- measured |>
  arrange(sample, z) |>
  group_by(group, sample) |>
  summarise(
    n             = n(),
    `local noise` = mad(diff(enamel_ratio)) / sqrt(2),
    `curve span`  = as.numeric(diff(quantile(enamel_ratio, c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(SNR = `curve span` / `local noise`,
         `threshold / noise` = params$outlier_abs / `local noise`)

noise_tbl |>
  mutate(`local noise` = round(`local noise`, 5),
         `curve span`  = round(`curve span`, 3),
         SNR           = round(SNR),
         `threshold / noise` = round(`threshold / noise`)) |>
  arrange(group, sample)
```

Two things follow, and they cut against the naive reading of these traces as "noisy":

1. **Local noise is 0.0012–0.0018 ratio units in every specimen**, knockout and wildtype alike. The
   absolute threshold of `r params$outlier_abs` is therefore ~45–65× the noise *uniformly*, so it
   does not need per-group scaling despite the CFTR curve spanning half the range of wildtype.
2. **Signal-to-noise exceeds 400 everywhere.** These traces carry almost no high-frequency scatter.
   What looks like noise in the CFTR ratio plot is **discontinuity** — gaps where slices are
   unmeasurable, and status changes between adjacent slices — not jitter. Sections 5 and 6 are
   built around that distinction.

### The rule

Reject a slice when its residual from **its own specimen's** trend exceeds `r params$outlier_abs`
ratio units. Per-specimen so a genuine between-animal offset is not scored as error; absolute so the
bar is identical for every specimen in every group.

```{r outliers}
fit_gam <- function(data, yvar = "enamel_ratio") {
  bam(reformulate(sprintf("s(z_percent, bs = 'tp', k = %d)", params$gam_k),
                  response = yvar),
      data = data, discrete = TRUE)
}

# Iteratively reweighted rejection: refit on the kept set, rescore, repeat until
# the kept set stops changing, so a gross outlier cannot drag the trend toward
# itself and mask its neighbours.
flag_outliers <- function(data, threshold = params$outlier_abs, max_iter = 10) {
  keep  <- rep(TRUE, nrow(data))
  resid <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  for (i in seq_len(max_iter)) {
    m     <- fit_gam(data[keep, , drop = FALSE])
    resid <- data$enamel_ratio - as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = data))
    new   <- abs(resid) <= threshold
    if (identical(new, keep)) break
    keep <- new
  }
  tibble(is_outlier = !keep, residual = resid)
}

scored <- measured |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  group_modify(~ bind_cols(.x, flag_outliers(.x))) |>
  ungroup()

clean <- scored |> filter(!is_outlier)

scored |>
  group_by(group, sample) |>
  summarise(n = n(), rejected = sum(is_outlier),
            `% rejected` = round(100 * mean(is_outlier), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(group, sample)
```

### Are the rejected slices independently bad?

The residual selected them, so the check has to use something the residual never saw — the
pipeline's own fit-quality statistics:

```{r outlier-evidence}
scored |>
  group_by(Slices = if_else(is_outlier, "rejected", "retained")) |>
  summarise(
    n                       = n(),
    `median separation (σ)` = round(median(separation_sigma, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `median d-statistic`    = round(median(d_statistic, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `median rim fraction`   = round(median(rim_fraction, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r outlier-location}
scored |>
  mutate(bin = cut(z_percent, breaks = seq(0, 100, 10),
                   labels = sprintf("%d–%d", seq(0, 90, 10), seq(10, 100, 10)),
                   include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  filter(is_outlier) |>
  count(group, bin) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

Rejections concentrate in the crossover region, where enamel and dentin densities are closest and
the two-component fit is hardest. That is the expected place for a mode-flip.

---

## 5. Where the curve is genuinely unmeasurable

Before smoothing anything, coverage has to be explicit: a smoother will happily interpolate across a
region where no measurement exists and present the result as data.

Coverage here means **"is there enamel to measure, and was it measured?"**, so `pre_onset` counts
as not measurable alongside `unresolvable`. The two are unmeasurable for opposite reasons —
`unresolvable` is a cross-section too thin to read, `pre_onset` is a cross-section read
successfully that contains no enamel — but for the purpose of deciding where a curve may be
drawn they are the same: there is no point on the mineralization curve at that z.

```{r coverage}
coverage <- profiles |>
  mutate(measurable = status %in% c("resolved_hi", "resolved_lo", "coincident"),
         bin = cut(z_percent, breaks = seq(0, 100, 10),
                   labels = sprintf("%d–%d", seq(0, 90, 10), seq(10, 100, 10)),
                   include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(group, sample, bin) |>
  summarise(pct_measurable = 100 * mean(measurable), .groups = "drop")

coverage |>
  group_by(group, bin) |>
  summarise(`% measurable` = round(mean(pct_measurable)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin, values_from = `% measurable`, values_fill = 0)
```

Coverage collapses at the cervical end in every group — that is the cervical loop, where there is
little mineralized tissue to measure. **Curves are therefore not extrapolated below the first
z-bin in which a group reaches 50 % mean coverage**, enforced in code rather than by eye:

```{r coverage-limit}
z_floor <- coverage |>
  group_by(group, bin) |>
  summarise(m = mean(pct_measurable), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(m >= 50) |>
  mutate(lo = as.numeric(str_extract(as.character(bin), "^[0-9]+"))) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(z_min = min(lo), .groups = "drop")

z_floor
```

---

## 6. Smoothing

The evidence in section 4 dictates the approach. SNR is >400, so there is little high-frequency
noise to remove and heavy smoothing would buy nothing while risking real structure. Smoothing is
therefore kept light, and the figures are built to **show gaps rather than bridge them**.

**Stage 1 — per-specimen rolling median.** A `r params$median_k`-slice centred median suppresses
single-slice spikes while preserving the steep crossover a mean would round off. `partial = FALSE`
so no values are fabricated at the ends, where the curve is steepest.

Crucially the window is defined in **slice index**, and is invalidated wherever it would span a gap,
so a run of missing slices is never silently bridged:

```{r smooth}
roll_med_gapped <- function(x, z, k) {
  if (length(x) < k) return(rep(NA_real_, length(x)))
  out <- zoo::rollapply(x, width = k, FUN = median, na.rm = TRUE,
                        fill = NA_real_, align = "center", partial = FALSE)
  # A centred window of width k is only meaningful if it covers k CONSECUTIVE
  # slices. Where z jumps, the window straddles a gap: drop it.
  zspan <- zoo::rollapply(z, width = k, FUN = function(v) max(v) - min(v),
                          fill = NA_real_, align = "center", partial = FALSE)
  out[is.na(zspan) | zspan > (k - 1) * 1.5] <- NA_real_
  out
}

smoothed <- clean |>
  arrange(sample, z) |>
  group_by(sample) |>
  mutate(
    ratio_med   = roll_med_gapped(enamel_ratio,   z, params$median_k),
    density_med = roll_med_gapped(enamel_density, z, params$median_k)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

smoothed |>
  group_by(group, sample) |>
  summarise(`slices in` = n(),
            `smoothed out` = sum(!is.na(ratio_med)),
            `dropped at gaps` = sum(is.na(ratio_med)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(group, sample)
```

**Stage 2 — GAM trend.** A penalized thin-plate spline across the specimens of a group gives that
group's consensus curve, restricted to the coverage floor from section 5.

```{r gam}
fit_trend <- function(data, yvar, n_out = 400, z_min = NULL) {
  data <- data |> filter(!is.na(.data[[yvar]]))
  if (!is.null(z_min) && is.finite(z_min)) data <- data |> filter(z_percent >= z_min)
  m <- gam(reformulate(sprintf("s(z_percent, bs = 'tp', k = %d)", params$gam_k),
                       response = yvar),
           data = data, method = "REML")
  grid <- tibble(z_percent = seq(min(data$z_percent), max(data$z_percent),
                                 length.out = n_out))
  grid |> mutate(fit = as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = grid)))
}

trend_by_group <- smoothed |>
  filter(!is.na(ratio_med)) |>
  left_join(z_floor, by = "group") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  group_modify(function(d, key) fit_trend(d, "ratio_med", z_min = d$z_min[1])) |>
  ungroup()
```

---

## 7. Confidence intervals and anatomy

**The unit of replication is the specimen, not the slice.** A tooth contributes ~1 100 slices, but
they are not 1 100 independent observations of its group: they come from one animal, one scan and
one dentin anchor, and the pipeline's `z_window` pooling correlates neighbours further.

The bands below are **cluster bootstraps**: resample the specimens of a group with replacement
`r params$n_boot` times, refit, take the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles. At n = 2–3 per group the
bootstrap has few distinct resamples, so these describe between-animal spread, **not** a
significance test.

```{r bootstrap}
boot_trend <- function(data, yvar, n_boot = params$n_boot, n_out = 400, z_min = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(z_min) && is.finite(z_min)) data <- data |> filter(z_percent >= z_min)
  data <- data |> filter(!is.na(.data[[yvar]]))
  ids  <- unique(data$sample)
  grid <- seq(min(data$z_percent), max(data$z_percent), length.out = n_out)
  fits <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = n_out)

  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    pick <- sample(ids, length(ids), replace = TRUE)
    d <- map_dfr(seq_along(pick),
                 \(i) data |> filter(sample == pick[i]) |> mutate(.rep = i))
    if (n_distinct(d$z_percent) < params$gam_k) next
    # bam(discrete = TRUE) is equivalent to gam() here and ~35x faster, which
    # is what makes a few hundred resamples practical.
    m <- try(bam(reformulate(sprintf("s(z_percent, bs = 'tp', k = %d)", params$gam_k),
                             response = yvar), data = d, discrete = TRUE),
             silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(m, "try-error")) next
    fits[b, ] <- as.numeric(predict(m, newdata = tibble(z_percent = grid)))
  }

  tibble(z_percent = grid,
         lower = apply(fits, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
         upper = apply(fits, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
}

set.seed(42)
bands <- smoothed |>
  filter(!is.na(ratio_med)) |>
  left_join(z_floor, by = "group") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  group_modify(function(d, key) boot_trend(d, "ratio_med", z_min = d$z_min[1])) |>
  ungroup()

trend_by_group <- trend_by_group |> left_join(bands, by = c("group", "z_percent"))
```

### Anatomical landmarks

`map_landmarks.py` marks the eruption plane and the mesial/distal boundaries of the three molars by
hand in napari on the reoriented volume, then maps them through the same CMPR centerline the density
profile uses. A landmark is a *z-plane*, so molars arrive as spans and eruption as a single event.

The landmark file's `z_percent` is used **as delivered**, and the delivered files were regenerated
on 2026-09-17 after a mirroring bug was fixed in `map_landmarks.py`.

That bug: `cmpr.py` does not promise which end of the incisor it starts tracing from, and on these
specimens it starts at the **tip**. `map_landmarks.py` nonetheless treated centerline index 0 as the
cervical loop, so every landmark came out mirrored — molars ordered M1, M2, M3 *away* from the
incisor and the eruption plane sitting cervical to all of them, which cannot happen. The fix detects
the tip end from mineralization (mature enamel is the densest tissue in the scan) and reports arc
length from the cervical loop so the two columns cannot disagree.

Correct anatomy, which the check below enforces: **M3 < M2 < M1 < eruption** in `z_percent`. M1 is
the mesial molar, nearest the incisor, and the tooth emerges in front of the whole molar row.

```{r landmark-load}
read_landmarks <- function(path) {
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
      sample = str_remove(basename(path), "_landmarks\\.csv$"),
      across(c(z_percent_start, z_percent_end, z_percent_mid, extent_percent,
               z_start, z_end, slice_start, slice_end,
               arc_length_start_mm, arc_length_end_mm, length_mm, z_residual_vox),
             ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))
    )
}

anat_all <- if (length(landmark_files) > 0) {
  map(landmark_files, read_landmarks) |> list_rbind()
} else tibble()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Landmark axis convention. READ THIS BEFORE "FIXING" IT.
#
# An earlier version of this report rewrote z_percent here, on the belief that
# map_landmarks.py had mirrored it by falling back to `tip-high-z`. That repair
# was wrong, and it silently reversed the molar order under every figure. The
# actual conventions are:
#
#   * `slice_start`/`slice_end` in the landmark file are CMPR CENTERLINE
#     indices, and they run cervical loop -> tip: arc_length_start_mm rises
#     monotonically with slice_start (eruption 4.5 mm @ 491, M3 10.3 mm @ 1148).
#     So z_percent = 100 * slice / (depth - 1), which is what the file already
#     contains.
#
#   * `z` in the density profile is a VOLUME index on the same resliced stack
#     (both are depth 1410 here) but the profile's own z_percent runs the other
#     way (corr(z, z_percent) = -1), because enamel_density.py labelled the
#     specimen `tip-low-z`.
#
# Those two facts are not in conflict: the profile already reports z_percent in
# trajectory order, and so does the landmark file. Re-deriving one from the
# other's orientation flag mixes the two index spaces and mirrors the result.
#
# The file's z_percent is therefore used as delivered. The check below is what
# catches a genuine mirroring, and it is now an independent test rather than a
# tautology: arc length must increase from cervical loop to tip.
if (nrow(anat_all) > 0) {
  anat_all <- anat_all |>
    left_join(profiles_all |>
                group_by(sample) |>
                summarise(depth = n_distinct(z), .groups = "drop"),
              by = "sample") |>
    mutate(
      # Spans are already stored in trajectory order by map_landmarks.py, but
      # normalise defensively so `extent` and the figures cannot be fed a
      # reversed span.
      z_percent_start = pmin(z_percent_start, z_percent_end, na.rm = TRUE),
      z_percent_end   = if_else(kind == "span",
                                pmax(z_percent_start, z_percent_end, na.rm = TRUE),
                                NA_real_),
      z_percent_mid   = if_else(kind == "span",
                                (z_percent_start + z_percent_end) / 2, z_percent_start),
      extent_percent  = if_else(kind == "span",
                                abs(z_percent_end - z_percent_start), NA_real_)
    ) |>
    left_join(meta, by = "sample") |>
    mutate(landmark = factor(landmark, levels = c("eruption", "M1", "M2", "M3")),
           group    = factor(paste(genotype, age), levels = group_levels)) |>
    arrange(sample, landmark)
}

anat <- anat_all |> filter(!sample %in% excluded)

if (nrow(anat) > 0) {
  anat |>
    distinct(group, sample, depth) |>
    transmute(group, sample, `depth (slices)` = depth) |>
    arrange(group, sample)
}
```

```{r landmark-sanity}
# Independent check that the landmark axis is not mirrored, using arc length --
# a quantity the z_percent conversion never touches. Arc length is measured
# from the cervical loop, so it must RISE with z_percent. If a future
# map_landmarks.py run does mirror the axis, this fails loudly instead of
# quietly reversing the molar order beneath every figure.
if (nrow(anat) > 0) {
  arc_ok <- anat |>
    filter(!is.na(arc_length_start_mm)) |>
    group_by(sample) |>
    filter(n() >= 3) |>
    summarise(rho = cor(z_percent_start, arc_length_start_mm), .groups = "drop")

  if (any(arc_ok$rho < 0.9)) {
    stop("Landmark z_percent disagrees with arc length in: ",
         paste(arc_ok$sample[arc_ok$rho < 0.9], collapse = ", "),
         ". The axis is mirrored -- see the convention note above.")
  }

  # Anatomical order along the tooth. M1 is the mesial molar, nearest the
  # incisor, so on this axis it sits TIPWARD of M2 and M3: M3 < M2 < M1. The
  # eruption plane is tipward of all three -- the tooth emerges in front of
  # the molar row.
  ord <- anat |>
    select(sample, landmark, z_percent_mid) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = landmark, values_from = z_percent_mid)
  stopifnot(all(ord$M3 < ord$M2, na.rm = TRUE),
            all(ord$M2 < ord$M1, na.rm = TRUE),
            all(ord$M1 < ord$eruption, na.rm = TRUE))

  tibble(check = c("arc length rises with z_percent (min rho)",
                   "M3 < M2 < M1 < eruption in all specimens"),
         value = c(sprintf("%.3f", min(arc_ok$rho)), "yes"))
}
```

```{r landmark-table}
if (nrow(anat) > 0) {
  anat |>
    transmute(group, sample, landmark, kind,
              `z start (%)`    = round(z_percent_start, 1),
              `z end (%)`      = round(z_percent_end, 1),
              `z mid (%)`      = round(z_percent_mid, 1),
              `extent (%)`     = round(extent_percent, 1),
              `length (mm)`    = round(length_mm, 2),
              `residual (vox)` = round(z_residual_vox, 2))
}
```

**The consensus is built per age, not pooled.** The incisor lengthens between P52 and P82 while the
molar row stays put in the jaw, so the same anatomical structure lands at a different `z_percent` at
the two ages. Averaging the ages together would place every landmark at a position that describes
neither, and it is the age axis (§11) and the development curve (§12) that would be read against
that wrong frame. Landmarks are therefore consensused within age, and every figure is drawn against
the strip for the age it shows. Genotype is deliberately *not* a stratifying variable here: a
knockout of enamel mineralization does not move the molars, so a landmark set is shared by all
specimens of an age, and pooling across genotype is what gives each age a usable n.

```{r landmark-consensus}
# Consensus within an arbitrary subset of `anat`. Used per age below, and by
# anat_strip() to draw the age-matched strip under each figure.
consensus_of <- function(d) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(tibble())
  d |>
    group_by(landmark, kind) |>
    summarise(n = n(),
              n_samples   = n_distinct(sample),
              start_mean  = mean(z_percent_start), end_mean  = mean(z_percent_end),
              mid_mean    = mean(z_percent_mid),
              start_min   = min(z_percent_start),  start_max = max(z_percent_start),
              end_min     = min(z_percent_end),    end_max   = max(z_percent_end),
              extent_mean = mean(extent_percent),  length_mean = mean(length_mm),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(mid_mean)
}

# One consensus per age that has any picks.
anat_by_age <- if (nrow(anat) > 0) {
  anat |>
    group_by(age) |>
    group_modify(function(d, key) consensus_of(d)) |>
    ungroup()
} else tibble()

# Which ages actually have landmarks, and which are still waiting on picks.
ages_present   <- sort(unique(meta$age))
ages_landmarked <- if (nrow(anat_by_age) > 0) sort(unique(anat_by_age$age)) else character(0)
ages_missing    <- setdiff(ages_present, ages_landmarked)

if (nrow(anat_by_age) > 0) {
  anat_by_age |>
    transmute(age, landmark, n = n_samples,
              `z start (%)` = round(start_mean, 1),
              `z end (%)`   = round(end_mean, 1),
              `z mid (%)`   = round(mid_mean, 1),
              `spread, start (%)` = if_else(is.na(start_min), NA_character_,
                                            sprintf("%.1f – %.1f", start_min, start_max)),
              `extent (%)`  = round(extent_mean, 1),
              `length (mm)` = round(length_mean, 2)) |>
    arrange(age, `z mid (%)`)
}
```

```{r landmark-coverage, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
# State the coverage in the report rather than in a comment: which ages have an
# age-matched strip, and which are currently drawn without one.
picked <- if (nrow(anat) > 0) {
  anat |> distinct(age, sample) |> count(age, name = "n") |>
    mutate(txt = sprintf("**%s**: %d specimen%s", age, n, if_else(n == 1, "", "s"))) |>
    pull(txt) |> paste(collapse = "; ")
} else "none"

cat(sprintf("> **Landmark coverage.** Picked so far — %s.\n", picked))
if (length(ages_missing) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0("> No landmarks yet for **%s**, so figures at that age are drawn with an ",
                     "empty anatomy strip and no eruption line rather than borrowing the other ",
                     "age's frame. Dropping those picks in and re-knitting fills them in with ",
                     "nothing else to change.\n"),
              paste(ages_missing, collapse = ", ")))
}
cat(paste0("> Within an age the landmark set is shared across genotypes by design. ",
           "Treat the strip as a reference frame, not as a per-group measurement, ",
           "until more specimens are picked.\n"))
```

```{r anat-layer, include = FALSE}
anat_levels <- c("eruption", "M1", "M2", "M3")

# Landmarks for ONE age. Every consumer below goes through this, so nothing can
# silently fall back to a pooled-across-age frame: an age with no picks yet
# returns an empty tibble and its figures are drawn without anatomy.
consensus_at <- function(ages) {
  if (nrow(anat_by_age) == 0) return(tibble())
  ages <- unique(ages[!is.na(ages)])
  # Only a single-age request can carry an age-matched frame. A figure spanning
  # two ages (the §11 age contrast, §13 orientation) gets no strip, because
  # there is no one anatomy that describes both.
  if (length(ages) != 1) return(tibble())
  anat_by_age |> filter(age == ages)
}

# Eruption plane for one age, NA when that age has no picks.
erupt_at <- function(ages) {
  d <- consensus_at(ages)
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  v <- d$mid_mean[d$landmark == "eruption"]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v[1]
}

# Age of a set of groups, as labelled in `meta`; length > 1 means mixed ages.
age_of_groups <- function(groups) {
  unique(meta$age[paste(meta$genotype, meta$age) %in% as.character(groups)])
}

# Reusable anatomy strip for one age. Dark bars are the mean molar extent, pale
# flanking blocks the range across the specimens of that age.
anat_strip <- function(ages = NULL) {
  ac <- consensus_at(ages)
  if (nrow(ac) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void() +
             labs(x = "Position along incisor (% length,  cervical loop → incisal tip)"))
  }
  spans <- ac |> filter(kind == "span")
  event <- ac |> filter(kind == "event")

  ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = spans,
              aes(xmin = start_min, xmax = end_max,
                  ymin = as.numeric(landmark) - 0.3, ymax = as.numeric(landmark) + 0.3),
              fill = "#1B7837", alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_rect(data = spans,
              aes(xmin = start_mean, xmax = end_mean,
                  ymin = as.numeric(landmark) - 0.3, ymax = as.numeric(landmark) + 0.3),
              fill = "#1B7837", alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_text(data = spans, aes(x = mid_mean, y = as.numeric(landmark), label = landmark),
              colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2) +
    geom_rect(data = event,
              aes(xmin = start_min, xmax = start_max,
                  ymin = as.numeric(landmark) - 0.3, ymax = as.numeric(landmark) + 0.3),
              fill = "#762A83", alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_segment(data = event,
                 aes(x = mid_mean, xend = mid_mean,
                     y = as.numeric(landmark) - 0.3, yend = as.numeric(landmark) + 0.3),
                 colour = "#762A83", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_text(data = event, aes(x = mid_mean, y = as.numeric(landmark), label = landmark),
              colour = "#762A83", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, hjust = -0.2) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                       guide = guide_prism_minor(), minor_breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL, limits = c(0.5, length(anat_levels) + 0.5)) +
    # Name the age on the strip itself, so a figure can never be read against an
    # anatomy frame whose age the reader has to infer.
    labs(x = "Position along incisor (% length,  cervical loop → incisal tip)", y = NULL,
         subtitle = sprintf("%s anatomy (n = %d)", ac$age[1], max(ac$n_samples))) +
    theme_prism(base_size = 11)
}

# Trajectory panel for an arbitrary set of groups. The eruption line is the one
# for the groups' age, and is omitted when they span ages or that age has no
# picks yet.
traj_panel <- function(groups, title = NULL) {
  erupt <- erupt_at(age_of_groups(groups))
  d <- trend_by_group |> filter(group %in% groups) |> droplevels()
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = z_percent, colour = group, fill = group)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.22, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(y = fit), linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, drop = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, drop = TRUE) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                       guide = guide_prism_minor(), minor_breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
    scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_prism_minor()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Enamel / dentin density ratio", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = title) +
    theme_prism(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  if (is.finite(erupt)) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = erupt, linetype = "longdash",
                        colour = "#762A83", linewidth = 0.6)
  }
  p
}

# Attach the anatomy strip for the age of the groups plotted. `ages` is passed
# explicitly by callers that already know it; otherwise derive it from groups.
with_anatomy <- function(p, ages = NULL, groups = NULL) {
  if (is.null(ages) && !is.null(groups)) ages <- age_of_groups(groups)
  p / anat_strip(ages) + plot_layout(heights = c(3, 1.1))
}

# Per-specimen trace figure, used by each comparison section.
sample_traces <- function(groups) {
  smoothed |>
    filter(group %in% groups, !is.na(ratio_med)) |>
    droplevels() |>
    ggplot(aes(z_percent, ratio_med, group = sample, colour = group)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                       guide = guide_prism_minor(), minor_breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
    labs(x = "Position along incisor (%)", y = "Enamel / dentin ratio", colour = NULL) +
    theme_prism(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}

# Crossover + plateau for a set of groups.
landmarks_of <- function(groups) {
  trend_by_group |>
    filter(group %in% groups) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    summarise(`crossover (z %)` = round(crossing_of(z_percent, fit), 1),
              `plateau ratio`   = round(plateau_of(z_percent, fit), 3),
              .groups = "drop")
}
```

---

## 8. The scans are comparable

Before any group is compared with another, the scans have to be on a shared intensity footing. Two
independent checks, neither of which depends on the incisor measurement itself.

```{r scanner-check}
molar_check <- map(json_files, function(path) {
  j <- jsonlite::fromJSON(path)
  m <- j$molar_cross_check
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  tibble(sample = j$sample,
         `molar dentin`   = round(m$dentin, 1),
         `molar enamel`   = round(m$enamel, 1),
         `separation (σ)` = round(m$separation, 2),
         `dentin anchor`  = round(j$anchor$mode, 1))
}) |> list_rbind()

profiles |>
  group_by(group, sample) |>
  summarise(`incisor dentin (median)` = round(median(dentin_reference, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(molar_check, by = "sample") |>
  arrange(group, sample)
```

The molar is fully mature in every animal regardless of group or age, so it must always separate
strongly — a weak molar would mean distrust the scan, not the biology. **Note that the CFTR molars
separate as well as wildtype molars.** The incisor phenotype in section 9 is therefore not a
scan-quality artifact: the same scan resolves that animal's molar enamel normally.

---

## 9. P82 WT vs P82 CFTR cKO

Age-matched and driver-matched: the only difference between these groups is the floxed *Cftr*
allele.

```{r fig-cftr, fig.height = 7.4, fig.cap = "Enamel/dentin density ratio, P82 wildtype (n = `r n_wt82`) against P82 CFTR cKO (n = `r n_cftr`), with anatomy on the shared axis. Bands are 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals over specimens. Dashed horizontal is dentin density; long-dashed vertical is the eruption plane."}
cftr_groups <- c("WT P82", "CFTR cKO P82")
with_anatomy(traj_panel(cftr_groups,
                        "P82 wildtype vs CFTR conditional knockout"),
             groups = cftr_groups)
```

```{r cftr-stats}
cftr_tbl <- landmarks_of(c("WT P82", "CFTR cKO P82"))
cftr_tbl
```

```{r cftr-prose, include = FALSE}
pl_wt   <- cftr_tbl$`plateau ratio`[cftr_tbl$group == "WT P82"]
pl_cf   <- cftr_tbl$`plateau ratio`[cftr_tbl$group == "CFTR cKO P82"]
pct_def <- round(100 * (1 - pl_cf / pl_wt))
```

**The CFTR knockout never reaches wildtype enamel density anywhere along the tooth.** Its mature
plateau is `r sprintf("%.2f", pl_cf)` against `r sprintf("%.2f", pl_wt)` in age-matched wildtype —
a **`r pct_def` % deficit** in the enamel/dentin ratio. The knockout curve rises only just above
dentin density, where wildtype reaches ~1.8×.

### Per-specimen traces

The group curve is only meaningful if every animal carries the effect:

```{r fig-cftr-by-sample, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Per-specimen smoothed traces. Gaps are genuine: the rolling median is set to NA wherever its window would span unmeasurable slices, so no segment is drawn across a region with no data."}
sample_traces(c("WT P82", "CFTR cKO P82"))
```

### Resolvability is itself the phenotype

Section 3 established that `coincident` slices must not be forced to 1.0. Their **prevalence**, and
the separation statistic behind it, is a direct readout of how distinguishable enamel is from dentin.

`% pre-enamel` is reported beside it but answers a different question. It is the share of the tooth
cervical to the enamel onset — where the pipeline found no enamel at all, rather than enamel it
could not separate from dentin — so it measures how far along the incisor enamel deposition has
got. Read the two together: a specimen can be low on one and high on the other, and only
`% coincident` speaks to mineralization quality.

```{r cftr-resolvability}
profiles |>
  filter(group %in% c("WT P82", "CFTR cKO P82")) |>
  group_by(group, sample) |>
  summarise(
    `% coincident`   = round(100 * mean(status == "coincident"), 1),
    `% pre-enamel`   = round(100 * mean(status == "pre_onset"), 1),
    `% unresolvable` = round(100 * mean(status == "unresolvable"), 1),
    `median separation (σ)` =
      round(median(separation_sigma[status %in% c("resolved_hi", "resolved_lo")],
                   na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(group, sample)
```

Wildtype enamel sits ~6.8 σ from dentin; CFTR enamel sits ~2.7 σ away and collapses below the
separation threshold on roughly a fifth of all slices. **The knockout's enamel is so
hypomineralized that it is frequently indistinguishable from dentin** — which is why its ratio plot
looks ragged, and why that raggedness is data rather than noise.

## 11. Age: P82 WT vs P52 WT

Both wildtype, both Odam-Cre, 30 days apart. This sets the scale for reading the knockout
comparisons: a genotype effect is only interesting if it exceeds what ordinary ageing does to the
same measurement.

```{r fig-age, fig.height = 7.4, fig.cap = "Enamel/dentin density ratio in wildtype at P52 (n = `r n_wt52`) and P82 (n = `r n_wt82`). Any displacement here is an age effect on a genotype-matched pair."}
# Two ages on one axis, so there is no single anatomy frame: with_anatomy()
# returns an empty strip here by design, and traj_panel() draws no eruption
# line. The per-age eruption planes are tabulated below instead.
with_anatomy(traj_panel(c("WT P52", "WT P82"), "Wildtype: P52 vs P82"),
             groups = c("WT P52", "WT P82"))
```

```{r age-stats}
landmarks_of(c("WT P52", "WT P82"))
```

```{r fig-age-by-sample, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Per-specimen smoothed traces for the two wildtype ages."}
sample_traces(c("WT P52", "WT P82"))
```

### Putting the three contrasts on one scale

The only way to read a genotype effect is against the age effect measured in the same units.

```{r contrast-table}
plateaus <- trend_by_group |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(plateau = plateau_of(z_percent, fit), .groups = "drop")

pget <- function(g) {
  v <- plateaus$plateau[plateaus$group == g]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v
}

tibble(
  contrast  = c("Age: P82 WT − P52 WT",
                "Genotype: CFTR cKO − P82 WT",
                "Genotype: Hif1a cKO − P52 WT"),
  reference = c(pget("WT P52"), pget("WT P82"), pget("WT P52")),
  delta     = c(pget("WT P82")       - pget("WT P52"),
                pget("CFTR cKO P82") - pget("WT P82"),
                pget("Hif1a cKO P52") - pget("WT P52"))
) |>
  transmute(contrast,
            `Δ plateau ratio` = round(delta, 3),
            `% of reference`  = round(100 * delta / reference, 1))
```

**Read the genotype rows against the age row.** If ageing 30 days moves the plateau by a small
fraction of what a knockout does, the knockout effect is not an age artifact.

---

## 12. The Odam-Cre wildtype development curve, by age

The wildtype Odam-Cre specimens give the reference trajectory for this driver line — the curve any
knockout is read against. **That reference is built separately at each age, not pooled.** Age is the
largest source of variation in a developmental profile: the incisor lengthens and the whole
mineralization sequence shifts along the `z_percent` axis between P52 and P82, so a curve averaged
over the two ages passes through the middle of a real displacement and describes neither age. It
would also be the wrong frame to read a knockout against, since each knockout is compared to its
age-matched wildtype in §9 and §10. The anatomy strip beneath each curve is likewise the one for
that age.

```{r wt-pool}
# One wildtype reference per age. Everything downstream -- landmarks, crossover,
# plateau, the figure -- is derived inside this per-age fit, so no quantity here
# is ever averaged across ages.
wt_ages <- smoothed |>
  filter(genotype == "WT", !is.na(ratio_med)) |>
  pull(age) |> unique() |> sort()

fit_wt_age <- function(a) {
  d <- smoothed |> filter(genotype == "WT", age == a, !is.na(ratio_med))
  # Coverage floor for this age's wildtype group only.
  floor_a <- z_floor |> filter(group == paste("WT", a)) |> pull(z_min)
  floor_a <- if (length(floor_a) == 0) NULL else max(floor_a)

  trend <- fit_trend(d, "ratio_med", z_min = floor_a)
  # Seeded per age so the band is reproducible regardless of which ages are run.
  set.seed(7)
  band  <- boot_trend(d, "ratio_med", z_min = floor_a)
  trend |> left_join(band, by = "z_percent") |> mutate(age = a, .before = 1)
}

wt_trend_by_age <- map(wt_ages, fit_wt_age) |> list_rbind()

# Interpolate the fitted ratio at an arbitrary z, within one age's curve.
ratio_at_age <- function(a, z) {
  d <- wt_trend_by_age |> filter(age == a)
  if (!is.finite(z) || nrow(d) == 0 ||
      z < min(d$z_percent) || z > max(d$z_percent)) return(NA_real_)
  approx(d$z_percent, d$fit, xout = z)$y
}

wt_summary <- map(wt_ages, function(a) {
  d     <- wt_trend_by_age |> filter(age == a)
  cross <- crossing_of(d$z_percent, d$fit)
  erupt <- erupt_at(a)
  tibble(
    age = a,
    n_specimens = n_distinct(smoothed$sample[smoothed$genotype == "WT" &
                                             smoothed$age == a]),
    crossover = cross,
    plateau   = plateau_of(d$z_percent, d$fit),
    eruption  = erupt,
    ratio_at_eruption = ratio_at_age(a, erupt),
    erupt_minus_cross = erupt - cross
  )
}) |> list_rbind()

wt_summary |>
  transmute(
    Age = age,
    `Specimens`                             = n_specimens,
    `Dentin-density crossover (z %)`        = sprintf("%.1f", crossover),
    `Mature plateau ratio (z 70–95 %)`      = sprintf("%.3f", plateau),
    `Eruption plane (z %)`                  = ifelse(is.na(eruption), "—",
                                                     sprintf("%.1f", eruption)),
    `Ratio at eruption`                     = ifelse(is.na(ratio_at_eruption), "—",
                                                     sprintf("%.2f", ratio_at_eruption)),
    `Eruption minus crossover (% length)`   = ifelse(is.na(erupt_minus_cross), "—",
                                                     sprintf("%+.1f", erupt_minus_cross))
  )
```

Each age's curve is drawn on its own, against its own anatomy.

```{r fig-wt-development, fig.height = 7.8, fig.cap = "Odam-Cre wildtype enamel development curve at each age, fitted separately. Band is the 95% cluster bootstrap over the specimens of that age. Dotted vertical marks the dentin-density crossover, long-dashed the eruption plane. The lower panel of each figure is that age's anatomy; an age with no landmark picks yet gets an empty strip rather than the other age's frame."}
wt_dev_plot <- function(a) {
  d     <- wt_trend_by_age |> filter(age == a)
  cross <- wt_summary$crossover[wt_summary$age == a]
  erupt <- wt_summary$eruption[wt_summary$age == a]
  ymin  <- min(d$fit, na.rm = TRUE)

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(z_percent)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "grey65", alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_line(aes(y = fit), linewidth = 1.3, colour = "#2166AC") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = cross, linetype = "dotted",
               colour = "#E08214", linewidth = 0.8) +
    annotate("text", x = cross, y = ymin, label = "crossover",
             angle = 90, vjust = 1.3, hjust = 0, colour = "#E08214", size = 3.4) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                       guide = guide_prism_minor(), minor_breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
    scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_prism_minor()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Enamel / dentin density ratio",
         title = sprintf("Odam-Cre wildtype enamel development — %s", a)) +
    theme_prism(base_size = 12)

  if (is.finite(erupt)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(xintercept = erupt, linetype = "longdash",
                 colour = "#762A83", linewidth = 0.7) +
      annotate("text", x = erupt, y = ymin, label = "eruption",
               angle = 90, vjust = -0.4, hjust = 0, colour = "#762A83", size = 3.4)
  }
  with_anatomy(p, ages = a)
}

for (a in wt_ages) print(wt_dev_plot(a))
```

```{r wt-dev-prose, include = FALSE}
# Prose below is generated from the per-age fits rather than hard-coded, so it
# cannot drift from the numbers when specimens or landmarks are added.
has_erupt <- wt_summary |> filter(is.finite(eruption))

intra_osseous <- if (nrow(has_erupt) > 0) {
  paste(sprintf(
    paste0("at **%s** the crossover sits at z = %.1f %% while the tooth does not emerge until ",
           "z = %.1f %%, with the fitted ratio already %.2f at the eruption plane"),
    has_erupt$age, has_erupt$crossover, has_erupt$eruption,
    has_erupt$ratio_at_eruption), collapse = "; ")
} else NA_character_

# Age displacement, stated only when both ages are actually present.
age_shift <- if (nrow(wt_summary) == 2) {
  o <- wt_summary |> arrange(age)
  sprintf("%.1f %% of length (%s: %.1f %%; %s: %.1f %%)",
          abs(diff(o$crossover)), o$age[1], o$crossover[1], o$age[2], o$crossover[2])
} else NA_character_

plateau_shift <- if (nrow(wt_summary) == 2) {
  o <- wt_summary |> arrange(age)
  sprintf("%.3f (%s: %.3f; %s: %.3f)",
          abs(diff(o$plateau)), o$age[1], o$plateau[1], o$age[2], o$plateau[2])
} else NA_character_
```

```{r wt-dev-text, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (!is.na(intra_osseous)) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "**Enamel reaches dentin density deep inside the bone, long before eruption.** In wildtype, ",
    "%s. Essentially all of amelogenesis — secretory, crossover and the steep maturation climb — ",
    "happens **intra-osseously**, on tissue never visible from outside the jaw. The consequence ",
    "for study design is direct: a phenotype anywhere in those phases is invisible on an erupted ",
    "or extracted crown, which is exactly where the CFTR deficit in section 9 lives.\n\n"),
    intra_osseous))
}

if (!is.na(age_shift)) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "**The two ages are separated on this axis, which is why they are not pooled.** The ",
    "crossover moves by %s between the two wildtype ages, and the mature plateau by %s. ",
    "A single pooled curve would sit between the two and describe neither; each knockout in ",
    "sections 9 and 10 is therefore read against the wildtype curve for its own age.\n"),
    age_shift, plateau_shift))
}
```

## 14. Sensitivity

Every headline number recomputed across the two tuning parameters that could plausibly drive it —
the outlier threshold and the median window.

```{r sensitivity, fig.height = 4.8, fig.cap = "Group plateau recomputed across outlier thresholds and median-window widths. Flat lines mean the landmark does not depend on the setting; what matters is that the groups keep their ordering and separation."}
sens_grid <- expand_grid(thr = c(0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.12, 0.20),
                         k   = c(11, 21, 31))

sens <- pmap_dfr(sens_grid, function(thr, k) {
  measured |>
    group_by(sample) |>
    group_modify(~ bind_cols(.x, flag_outliers(.x, threshold = thr))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(!is_outlier) |>
    arrange(sample, z) |>
    group_by(sample) |>
    mutate(rm = roll_med_gapped(enamel_ratio, z, k)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(!is.na(rm)) |>
    left_join(z_floor, by = "group") |>
    group_by(group) |>
    group_modify(function(d, key) {
      tr <- fit_trend(d, "rm", z_min = d$z_min[1])
      tibble(plateau   = plateau_of(tr$z_percent, tr$fit),
             crossover = crossing_of(tr$z_percent, tr$fit))
    }) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(thr = thr, k = k)
})

ggplot(sens, aes(thr, plateau, colour = group, linetype = factor(k))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols) +
  labs(x = "Outlier threshold (ratio units)", y = "Mature plateau ratio",
       colour = NULL, linetype = "median k") +
  theme_prism(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r sensitivity-table}
sens |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(`plateau min`         = round(min(plateau, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `plateau max`         = round(max(plateau, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `plateau range`       = round(max(plateau, na.rm = TRUE) -
                                            min(plateau, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `crossover range (%)` = round(max(crossover, na.rm = TRUE) -
                                            min(crossover, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop")
```

If the plateau range within a group is small against the between-group differences in section 11,
no conclusion in this report depends on the tuning.

### The `coincident` rule is the one choice that does matter

Section 3 showed this directly. Unlike the outlier threshold and the median width, **this setting
changes the CFTR curve materially**, which is why it is a named parameter with a documented default
rather than a buried constant.

out_dir <- file.path(params$figure_dir, "..", "exports")

  mutate(`size (KB)` = round(file.size(file.path(out_dir, file)) / 1024, 1))
